Title: Geschichtschreiber der husitischen Bewegung in Böhmen, herausgegeben von Dr. K. Höfler. Theil II (Fontes rerum Austriacarum, Scriptores VI)
Creator: Constantin von Höfler (1811-1897), editor; includes the Chronicon Taboritarum of John of Lukavec and Nicholas of Pelhřimov (Biskupec).
Publisher: Wien: aus der k. k. Hof- und Staatsdruckerei (Fontes rerum Austriacarum, Erste Abtheilung, Scriptores, VI. Band)
Publication Date: 1865
Rights: Public Domain
Rights basis: the title page of this scan reads 'THEIL II' and a year whose last digit the OCR garbles ('186S'; elsewhere in the file '1863'); the item record and the other scan of the same volume (geschichtschreib02hofl) give 1865, and the editor's preface dates the work to 1863 or later; every reading is before 1930; the item record carries the Public Domain Mark 1.0 licence.
Language: lat (mixed: Latin and some German; Höfler's German notes)
Source: Internet Archive item bub_gb_AnOWDr0KmJYC (archive.org/details/bub_gb_AnOWDr0KmJYC), full-text file bub_gb_AnOWDr0KmJYC_djvu.txt, fetched directly by the Library thread, October 2026.
Provenance note: Header prepended by the Library thread; the OCR text follows unchanged apart from this header. Nothing stripped, normalised, corrected, re-spaced or retyped. Sampled at opening, middle and end: Latin readable with scattered letter errors and a few garbled pages. The word-form coverage against clean Latin is 0.74 here against 0.68 for the other scan of the same volume (geschichtschreib02hofl), which is why this scan was taken.
Content note: Höfler's second volume, 24 numbered items, among them the 'Chronicon Taboritarum' of John of Lukavec and Nicholas of Pelhřimov (called Biskupec), the Taborite priests' account of their case against the Prague masters, with the priests' 'Responsio ... ad scriptum magistrorum' (item XXIV). The Chronicon prints the Taborite priests' five articles (printed pp. 478-479, said to have been preached to the mountain gathering of 1419: priests holding no land or rents by civil title, tithes as freely given support and not a debt, priests giving up civil lordship, the Gospel law as sufficient for the church without the old-law ceremonies and added rites, and flight from thieves and robbers who climb in by another way), a footnote at the foot of p. 700 marks the end of the 'confessio Thaboritarum' (the Chronicon's first part) and cites p. 503 of a Rotterdam printing of 1616, and Part II (printed p. 701 ff.) tells the Bohemians' hearing at the Council of Basel on the four articles of Prague; the 'Tractatus de origine Hussitarum' (item XIX), a Catholic polemic that names the Adamites and the Taborites; Hus's letters and the Prague university papers. The strongest inside Taborite text found, and the nearest the shelf has to the Taborite articles and the Four Articles of Prague as the Hussites argued them; the Chronicon is a Taborite document, the Tractatus a hostile one. No public-domain English translation is vendored.
